sources.entry: GhostVM - Virtualization tool for creating and managing isolated macOS virtual machine workspaces. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: GhostVM is a native macOS app for creating and managing isolated macOS virtual machines on Apple Silicon using Apple's Virtualization.framework, with each VM stored as a portable .GhostVM bundle.
summary.what_it_does: GhostVM provides a SwiftUI macOS app for creating, installing, starting, and managing macOS guest VMs on Apple Silicon. Each VM is a self-contained .GhostVM bundle that can be copied, moved, or backed up like a file. It supports snapshots and clones, with the README saying clones use APFS copy-on-write. A vmctl command-line tool covers init, install, start, stop, suspend, resume, status, snapshot management, and listing VMs. Remote commands (exec, clipboard get/set, apps) require GhostTools installed in the guest. The README also describes clipboard sync, file transfer, shared folders via VirtioFS, NAT networking, and automatic port forwarding.
use_cases: Sandboxing AI agents in an isolated macOS environment
Isolating client work in separate VMs
Scripting VM control through a CLI or Unix socket API
how_to_run: Download the latest DMG from the releases page
Open the DMG and drag GhostVM.app to Applications
Launch GhostVM and create your first workspace
git clone the repository, cd GhostVM, then run make app
Use vmctl init, install, and start to create and boot a VM
notable: Self-contained .GhostVM bundles that are portable like ordinary files
Snapshots and clones using APFS copy-on-write
Full CLI (vmctl) and Unix socket API for automation
VirtioFS shared folders and NAT networking via Apple's framework
GhostTools guest agent for clipboard, file transfer, and port discovery
caveats: Requires macOS 15+ (Sequoia) on Apple Silicon (M1 or later)
Source code license not yet determined; only the signed DMG is stated as free to use
Apple's EULA requires macOS guests to run on Apple-branded hardware
